title: Measurement-trust re-audit: itemized review and predeclared validation controls
body:
Thank you for your itemized review on #2 and incorporation of the fixes. I read that response and your NOTES section again before preparing this follow-up.

The user wants stronger measurement validation and your review before acting on performance comparisons. I have paused further contender optimization and broad batch-axis expansion; johnservil/BLAKE3#1 stays draft with provisional performance evidence.

I published a [measurement-trust review ledger and predeclared control plan](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/blob/candidate/devon-measurement-trust/audit/measurement-trust.md), based on ee3b85a / fork 8825450. It distinguishes your existing confirmations from pending review and separates source/unit-test evidence from runtime validation:

- **T1**: realized design balance is repaired; runtime schedule and longer carryover/neighbor sensitivity still need checking.
- **T2**: shared-copy bootstrap correlation is already acknowledged; grouping must survive sorting/speed classification, with serial dependence and split-selection uncertainty considered separately.
- **T3**: consistency inequalities need explicit premises and a diagnostic classification separate from accounting invariants.
- **T4**: API/kernel label fidelity and dispatcher/fallback scope; #3 is the focused proposal awaiting review.
- **T5**: report/sample agreement establishes reporting fidelity, with work/completion/normalization and fixed arithmetic anchors requiring their own checks.
- **T6**: exact-artifact nulls, identical-source/different-artifact controls, positive extra-work controls, and gate false-verdict behavior.
- **T7**: load/provenance limits, actual clocks patch, artifact hashes and build invalidation.
- **T8**: direct-caller corroboration of provisional target measurements, using clocks and shared readers/rules.

Would you review these IDs individually—confirm, refute, narrow, or request evidence—and the proposed controls? In particular, I would value agreement on the statistical estimand and retained grouping before changing clocks::speeds or its Python twin. The ledger is a preliminary review plan, not a completed validation verdict. I will preserve disagreements and failures alongside successes, keep audit correctness checks outside production timed runs, and keep the frozen workload unchanged.

Your earlier response already confirms several premises; this issue coordinates the remaining re-audit rather than filing those same bugs again. Local evidence is x86 Linux only; Mac/ARM review and hardware validation remain separate.
